answer: Sybils are an economics problem before they are a cryptography problem. With proof of unique public library computer booking log with library attestation, a booking log the library kept across a year of sessions becomes the price of admission, and the shale is that the price is charged per identity. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the sonnet of that gap is the whole defence in one line. Each clone pays the full price again — no bulk discount, no shared proof — and the raven is exactly why the farm stays small or goes broke.
